functions: Describing the benefits of video conferencing (Video conferencing)
grammarFocus: Describing current changes: present continuous; more and more + noun; comparative + and + comparative; get/become + comparative adjective; increase, decrease, go up, go down
Second conditional: If + past simple, would/could + infinitive (situations that are not true now or are unlikely)
Giving meanings of technical words: brackets, called, be, a separate sentence, relative clause (which/that/who)
Making requests: It would be great to know…, I'd like/love to know…, Could someone tell me…?, can/could

parts.instructions: Listen to the conversation and choose the best answer A, B, C or D (Questions L1–L5).
parts.context: Kate, the manager of a garden supplies company, talks to Tom, a web developer, about building an online shop.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Hi Kate. You said on the phone that you want to start selling online. Why now?

script.speaker: Kate
script.text: Well, sales in our two shops are going down every month. At the same time, more and more customers are phoning us to ask if they can order from home.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: That's a very common trend. So, an online shop has three main parts. The first part is the user interface, which is everything the customer sees on the screen.

script.speaker: Kate
script.text: Is that the most difficult part to build?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Not really, but it's very important. It has to look good and be easy to use. If it's confusing, people leave before they buy anything.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: That's the second part, the payment processing system. It takes the customer's card details and delivery address. When the payment goes through, it sends the order straight to your warehouse team, so they can pack it the same day.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: An order tracking page, called "Where's my order?", where customers can check their delivery.

script.speaker: Kate
script.text: Should the site work on phones too?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Definitely. Nowadays more people are shopping on their phones than on laptops, so it must work well on small screens.

script.speaker: Kate
script.text: OK. How long will it all take?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: The design takes about two weeks. I think the first version will be ready in six weeks.

questions.stem: Why does Kate want to start an online shop?

options.text: Her staff want to work from home.
Sales in her shops are going down.
Her shops are closing next year.

questions.explanation: Kate nói "sales in our two shops are going down every month" (doanh số ở hai cửa hàng giảm mỗi tháng). Bài không nói nhân viên muốn làm ở nhà, cửa hàng sắp đóng hay phí giao hàng rẻ hơn.

questions.stem: What does Tom say about the user interface?

options.text: It is the most difficult part to build.
It sends orders to the warehouse.
It is only needed on mobile phones.
It must look good and be easy to use.

questions.explanation: Tom nói giao diện "has to look good and be easy to use". Khi Kate hỏi đó có phải phần khó nhất không, Tom trả lời "Not really", nên A sai. Gửi đơn đến kho là việc của hệ thống xử lý thanh toán (B sai).

questions.stem: What happens when a customer's payment goes through?

options.text: The order goes to the warehouse team.
The customer gets a paper receipt.
Kate phones the customer to check.
The system deletes the card details.

questions.explanation: Tom nói khi thanh toán xong, hệ thống "sends the order straight to your warehouse team" để nhân viên kho đóng gói trong ngày. Các phương án còn lại không được nhắc đến.

questions.stem: Why must the website work well on phones?

options.text: Phones are getting cheaper every year.
More people shop on phones than on laptops.
Tom only builds apps for phones.

questions.explanation: Tom nói "more people are shopping on their phones than on laptops" (ngày càng nhiều người mua sắm bằng điện thoại hơn máy tính xách tay), nên trang web phải chạy tốt trên màn hình nhỏ.

questions.stem: When will the first version of the online shop be ready?
questions.explanation: Tom nói "the first version will be ready in six weeks". Hai tuần là thời gian thiết kế, còn thứ Hai tới là ngày bắt đầu làm, không phải ngày xong.

parts.instructions: Listen to the announcement and answer the questions. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each answer (Questions L6–L10).
parts.context: David, an IT trainer, gives staff information about training sessions on the company's new enterprise social networking system.

script.speaker: David
script.text: Good morning, everyone. This is David from the IT Training Team. Thank you for all your requests for training on our new enterprise social networking system. Many of you wrote, "It would be great to know how to find old messages," so we are organising two short sessions.

script.speaker: David
script.text: The first session is on Tuesday at ten o'clock in Training Room 2, on the third floor. Each session lasts forty-five minutes. In this session, we will look at threaded view, which groups all the messages from one conversation together, so you can read them like a chat. We will also practise tagging, that is, adding keywords to messages and files so that they are easy to find in a search.

script.speaker: David
script.text: The second session is on Thursday afternoon, and it is about smartphone syncing. More and more of you are working away from the office, so you need the same information on your phone and on your computer. Please bring your smartphone to this session, and make sure it is fully charged.

script.speaker: David
script.text: There are only twelve places in each session. If you'd like to join, could you send an email to the IT help desk by Monday? Thank you.

questions.stem: On which day is the first training session?
questions.explanation: David nói "The first session is on Tuesday at ten o'clock". Buổi thứ hai mới là thứ Năm (Thursday).

questions.stem: In which room is the first session?
questions.explanation: Buổi đầu tiên ở "Training Room 2, on the third floor" (phòng đào tạo số 2, tầng ba).

questions.stem: Which feature groups all the messages from one conversation together?
questions.explanation: David giải thích "threaded view, which groups all the messages from one conversation together". Tagging là gắn từ khoá để dễ tìm, không phải gom tin nhắn theo cuộc hội thoại.

questions.stem: What should staff bring to the second session?
questions.explanation: David nói "Please bring your smartphone to this session", vì buổi thứ hai học đồng bộ dữ liệu giữa điện thoại và máy tính (smartphone syncing).

questions.stem: How many places are there in each session?
questions.explanation: David nói "There are only twelve places in each session" (mỗi buổi chỉ có 12 chỗ). Số 45 là thời lượng mỗi buổi (forty-five minutes), không phải số chỗ.

matching.instructions: Match the terms (1–5) with the correct definitions (A–F). There is one extra definition that you do not need (Questions 1–5).

definitions.text: A technology that lets two nearby devices exchange data.
An online place where customers keep items before paying.
Software used to organise, store and share company documents.
A service for posting very short updates.
A method of making a digital file smaller.
A system that controls how purchased digital content can be used.

items.explanation: Microblogging system là hệ thống blog vi mô, dùng để đăng các cập nhật rất ngắn (ví dụ Twitter).
Data compression (nén dữ liệu) là cách làm cho tệp nhỏ lại để dễ lưu trữ và gửi đi.
Shopping basket (giỏ hàng) là nơi trên trang web mà khách hàng để sản phẩm vào trước khi thanh toán.
Document management system (hệ thống quản lý tài liệu) là phần mềm dùng để sắp xếp, lưu trữ và chia sẻ tài liệu của công ty.
NFC (Near Field Communication, giao tiếp trường gần) cho phép hai thiết bị ở rất gần nhau trao đổi dữ liệu. Định nghĩa F là của DRM (Digital Rights Management), không có trong danh sách thuật ngữ.

grammar.stem: The number of employees using our company network ______ this year.
grammar.explanation: Mô tả thay đổi đang diễn ra dùng hiện tại tiếp diễn. Chủ ngữ "The number of …" là số ít nên dùng "is increasing", không dùng "are".

grammar.stem: Staff are becoming ______ interested in online document collaboration.
grammar.explanation: Cấu trúc mô tả xu hướng: become + "more and more" + tính từ (ngày càng …). Các phương án còn lại sai cấu trúc.

grammar.stem: If we ______ high-definition cameras, our overseas meetings would be clearer.
grammar.explanation: Câu điều kiện loại 2: mệnh đề chính có "would be" nên mệnh đề "if" dùng quá khứ đơn "bought".

grammar.stem: If we moved the intranet to a faster server, staff ______ less time waiting for pages to load.
grammar.explanation: Câu điều kiện loại 2: mệnh đề "if" ở quá khứ đơn (moved) nên mệnh đề chính dùng would + động từ nguyên mẫu: "would spend".

grammar.stem: Our shop sends order data to the accounting system in a standard format ______ EDI (Electronic Data Interchange).
grammar.explanation: Khi giải nghĩa thuật ngữ, dùng "called" + tên thuật ngữ (dạng bị động rút gọn: a format which is called EDI). "calling" mang nghĩa chủ động nên sai.

grammar.stem: Could someone tell me how ______ a refund in the new order system?
grammar.explanation: Yêu cầu lịch sự "Could someone tell me how + to V …?". Sau "how" trong cấu trúc này dùng "to process".

grammar.stem: It would be great ______ how to create a new group in the company forum.
grammar.explanation: Yêu cầu lịch sự "It would be great + to V": "It would be great to know …" (Thật tốt nếu được biết …).

vocabulary.stem: Online shops store small ______ on your computer so that the website recognises you on your next visit.
vocabulary.explanation: Cookie là mẩu dữ liệu nhỏ mà trang web lưu trên máy tính của bạn để nhận ra bạn khi bạn quay lại. Graph (đồ thị), forum (diễn đàn), trend (xu hướng) không phù hợp.

vocabulary.stem: As well as our website, we have four ______ shops where customers can see the products face-to-face.
vocabulary.explanation: Bricks and mortar shop là cửa hàng có địa điểm thực, khách đến mua trực tiếp, khác với cửa hàng chỉ có trên mạng.

vocabulary.stem: In a video conference, the ______ participants are in the same room as you, while the others join from different locations.
vocabulary.explanation: Local participants là những người tham gia ở cùng địa điểm với bạn. Remote participants là người tham gia từ xa, trái nghĩa với vế "in the same room as you".

vocabulary.stem: The new chat tool will ______ with our email and calendar software, so staff can use all three together.
vocabulary.explanation: Integrate (with) nghĩa là tích hợp, kết hợp để các phần cùng hoạt động hiệu quả. Vế "so staff can use all three together" cho thấy cần nghĩa này.
B2B (Business to Business) là hoạt động kinh doanh giữa các công ty với nhau, thường qua Internet. B2C là Business to Consumer.

vocabulary.stem: An MCU is used to connect several ______ locations at the same time.
vocabulary.explanation: MCU (Multipoint Control Unit) là thiết bị kết nối nhiều điểm hội nghị truyền hình cùng lúc.

vocabulary.stem: E-commerce companies use ______ to protect customers' card details when they are sent over the internet.
vocabulary.explanation: Encryption (mã hoá) biến dữ liệu thành mã để người khác không đọc được, dùng để bảo vệ thông tin thẻ. Tagging là gắn nhãn, archiving là lưu trữ tệp cũ, syncing là đồng bộ.

vocabulary.stem: With ______ recognition, staff can give commands to the system by speaking instead of typing.
vocabulary.explanation: Voice recognition (nhận dạng giọng nói) là khả năng máy tính nhận ra lời nói. Vế "by speaking" chỉ ra đáp án.

passageMcq.instructions: Read the passage and choose the best answer A, B, C or D (Questions 21–25).

passage.title: Connecting Teams at Linden Systems
paragraphs: Linden Systems is a medium-sized IT company with offices in three countries. In the past, employees in different departments communicated mainly by long email chains. Important messages were often difficult to find, and staff in one office rarely knew who in another office could answer their questions. Last year, the managers decided to introduce an enterprise social networking system.

The new system provides instant messaging, forums and profile pages. Staff use instant messaging to ask quick questions, while the forums are useful for longer discussions about projects. Every employee also has a profile page that shows their job, their skills and the projects they are working on. This means that it is now easy to find the right person to ask, even in another country.

Since the system was introduced, the way people communicate has changed. The number of internal emails is going down every month, and more and more staff are using the forums to work with colleagues in the overseas departments. Many teams say they are getting answers much faster than before. The system is also becoming more popular with managers, who now use it to post company announcements.

However, there are still some problems. Many employees work away from the office when they visit customers, and at the moment they cannot use the system on their phones. The IT department will introduce a mobile app next month so that staff can read messages and join discussions wherever they are.

questions.stem: Why did Linden Systems introduce an enterprise social networking system?

options.text: To make communication between staff easier
To reduce the number of employees

questions.explanation: Đoạn 1 nêu vấn đề: nhân viên giao tiếp chủ yếu bằng chuỗi email dài, khó tìm tin nhắn quan trọng, không biết ai ở văn phòng khác có thể trả lời câu hỏi. Vì vậy công ty đưa vào hệ thống mạng xã hội doanh nghiệp để giao tiếp giữa nhân viên dễ hơn.

questions.stem: What do employees mainly use instant messaging for?
questions.explanation: "Staff use instant messaging to ask quick questions". Thảo luận dài dùng forum; thông báo công ty do quản lý đăng (đoạn 3).

questions.stem: How can staff now find the right colleague to answer a question?
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: trang hồ sơ (profile page) cho biết công việc, kỹ năng và dự án của từng người, nên "it is now easy to find the right person to ask". Chuỗi email dài là cách cũ; ứng dụng di động tháng sau mới có (D sai).

questions.stem: What is happening to the number of internal emails?

options.text: It is going down every month.

questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: "The number of internal emails is going down every month" (số email nội bộ giảm mỗi tháng).

questions.stem: What will the IT department do next month?
questions.explanation: Đoạn 4: "The IT department will introduce a mobile app next month" để nhân viên dùng hệ thống trên điện thoại khi đi gặp khách hàng.

passageTrueFalse.instructions: Read the passage and write T (True) or F (False) (Questions 26–30).

passage.title: Choosing a Video Meeting System
paragraphs: A small design firm has two offices in different cities. Its manager is deciding whether to buy videophones or a complete video conferencing system. A videophone is cheaper and is useful when only two people need to speak. However, the design team often needs to hold meetings with several people at different locations. For this reason, a complete system may be more suitable.

The proposed system would connect more than two locations. It includes high-definition monitors, cameras and a control panel, and it needs a dedicated room. The equipment cannot be kept in a shared office, so the firm will turn one of its meeting rooms into a video conferencing room. If the firm bought the system, staff would be able to discuss designs without travelling as often. The initial price is higher than the price of videophones, but the manager expects fewer business trips to reduce costs in the long term.
Before making a final decision, the manager wants more information about maintenance costs and training. She knows that employees will need to learn how to operate the new equipment correctly.

questions.statement: A videophone is the cheaper option for the firm.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 1: "A videophone is cheaper". Đoạn 2 cũng nói giá ban đầu của hệ thống đầy đủ cao hơn giá videophone.

questions.statement: The design team always holds meetings with exactly two people.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 1: nhóm thiết kế thường họp với "several people at different locations", không phải luôn chỉ hai người.

questions.statement: The equipment for the complete system can be kept in a shared office.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2 nói rõ "The equipment cannot be kept in a shared office" (không được đặt thiết bị trong văn phòng dùng chung); công ty sẽ chuyển một phòng họp thành phòng hội nghị truyền hình riêng.

questions.statement: The manager believes the complete system could save money over time.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: quản lý kỳ vọng ít chuyến công tác hơn sẽ "reduce costs in the long term" (giảm chi phí về lâu dài).

questions.statement: The manager is not interested in training needs.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: quản lý muốn có thêm thông tin về chi phí bảo trì và đào tạo, và biết nhân viên cần học cách dùng thiết bị.

items.source: The number of employees using our enterprise social networking system is increasing steadily.
items.referenceTranslation: Số lượng nhân viên sử dụng hệ thống mạng xã hội doanh nghiệp của chúng tôi đang tăng đều đặn.

items.source: If we had a video conferencing system, we would spend less money on business travel.
items.referenceTranslation: Nếu chúng tôi có hệ thống hội nghị truyền hình, chúng tôi sẽ tốn ít tiền hơn cho các chuyến công tác.

items.source: Data compression reduces the size of files, so they need less bandwidth when they are sent.
items.referenceTranslation: Nén dữ liệu làm giảm kích thước tệp, vì vậy khi được gửi đi, các tệp cần ít băng thông hơn.

items.source: A document management system allows employees to store, share and find company files.
items.referenceTranslation: Hệ thống quản lý tài liệu cho phép nhân viên lưu trữ, chia sẻ và tìm kiếm các tệp của công ty.

items.source: Could you tell me how to archive old messages in the company system?
items.referenceTranslation: Bạn có thể cho tôi biết cách lưu trữ các tin nhắn cũ trong hệ thống của công ty không?

email.task:
You are an IT support technician. Tomorrow a new employee, Hana, will join a video conference with the company's overseas office for the first time. Write an email explaining how to join the video conference, using the steps below. End the email with a reminder. In your email you must use:
- at least one polite request (Could you…? / It would be great if you could…), for example asking Hana to come early to test the equipment;
- at least one second conditional sentence (If + past simple, … would + verb), for example to explain what would happen if the remote participants heard background noise.
Write 80–100 words.
bullets: switch on the video conferencing equipment
check the camera and microphone connections
enter the meeting ID and select “Join”
check that remote participants appear on the screen
mute the microphone when you are not speaking
leave the meeting and switch off the equipment
targetGrammar: Polite requests (at least one): Could you…?, It would be great if you could…, can/could
Second conditional (at least one), for example in the reminder: If + past simple, would + infinitive
Imperatives with sequence words (first, then, next, finally) for the steps
email.modelAnswer:
Dear Hana,

Here is how to join tomorrow's video conference. First, switch on the video conferencing equipment and check the camera and microphone connections. Then open the conferencing application, enter the meeting ID and select “Join”. Next, check that the remote participants appear on the screen. Please mute your microphone when you are not speaking. Finally, leave the meeting and switch off the equipment.

Just a reminder: could you come ten minutes early to test the equipment? If the remote participants heard noise from our room, they would not understand the speakers.

Best regards,
Minh
IT Support

parts.instructions: Answer the three questions. Speak for 30–45 seconds for each question.
questions: How are you and your friends communicating online these days? Describe one way that is becoming more popular and one way that is becoming less popular. Use the present continuous and phrases such as more and more, is getting/becoming + comparative, or is going up/down.

Imagine your university has just started using a new online learning system. What would you like to learn about it? Make at least two polite requests for training, using It would be great to know…, I'd like to know… or Could someone tell me…?
If your university had a video conferencing system for all classes, how would your studies be different? Answer with the second conditional (If + past simple, … would + verb).

parts.instructions: Explain the terms to a colleague. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: A new colleague in the sales department is reading a report about your company's online shop but does not understand some e-commerce terms. Explain what each term in the cues means and give an example for each one. Give the meanings in at least two different spoken ways: called, which means, or is.
cues: Ways to give meanings: … called …, … which means …, … is …
requiredGrammar: Giving meanings with called: a business model called bricks and clicks
Giving meanings with which means / a relative clause: B2C, which means business to consumer, …
Giving meanings with be: DRM is…
parts.sampleAnswer: Let me explain four terms from the report. First, B2C, which means business to consumer, is selling directly to ordinary customers on the internet. Our online shop is a B2C system because we sell to the public, not to other companies. Second, we use a business model called bricks and clicks. A bricks and clicks company has both real shops and an online shop, like a supermarket that also sells on its website. Third, DRM is Digital Rights Management. It is a method that limits how people can use digital content after they buy it. For example, you can't copy some e-books to another device. Finally, there is encryption, which is a way of changing data into a code so that nobody else can read it. Online shops use encryption to protect customers' card details when they pay.

parts.instructions: Deal with the situation. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: You are an IT officer at a travel company. At the monthly meeting, your manager asks you how communication with customers and staff is changing. Use the cues to describe the current trends. Use the present continuous, more and more, get/become + comparative, and verbs such as increase, decrease, go up and go down. Then suggest one thing the company should do.
cues: customer emails to the help desk: going down
customers using live chat on the website: more and more
the current enterprise social network: getting slower
requiredGrammar: Present continuous for changes happening now: Customer emails are going down.
more and more + noun / comparative + and + comparative
get/become + comparative adjective: The system is getting slower.
increase, decrease, go up, go down
parts.sampleAnswer: Thank you. I'd like to describe some current trends in how people communicate with our company. First, customer emails to the help desk are going down. At the same time, more and more customers are using the live chat on our website, because it is faster for them. Inside the company, the number of staff working from home is increasing, so they need good access to our systems from outside the office. However, our enterprise social network is getting slower and slower, and staff are becoming more frustrated with it. Voice recognition is also becoming more popular, and many staff want to give commands by speaking. Because of these trends, I think we should upgrade the network soon and add a mobile app for staff who work away from the office.
